summary: This is a bash function that pulls staged git changes and sends them to an AI model for code review. It asks the AI to check for SOLID violations, magic constants, long functions, naming issues, and overall quality problems, then prints the AI's feedback directly to the terminal without modifying anything.

explanations.5: This line registers the ai-review command in a lookup table so the user can invoke it by name; the description explains what it does.
explanations.6: This stores that the review command takes no additional parameters, so the calling code knows not to expect arguments.
explanations.10: This runs a helper function to extract just the staged changes (the parts git will commit) and stores them in the diff variable, or exits early if that fails.
explanations.12: This creates a long string that will be sent to the AI, telling it exactly how to structure its response with specific headings and instructions to avoid making up problems.
explanations.25: This sends the full prompt (instructions plus the actual code diff) to the AI model and prints whatever it replies.
